coaches._note: What to call each coach. The export keys everything to an email address; this is the only place that decides what gets printed. A coach with no entry falls back to the part of their address before the @, so a new hire is readable on day one.
coaches._excludeFromBoards: Coaches in the network but not in the internal competition. Separate from monitoring.ignoreGroups, which is about whole teams nobody coaches.

month._note: Month-on-month works from the first upload: it compares two complete months, so it needs no daily readings.

ramp._target: 200,000 diamonds inside a single calendar month. The first 90 days give roughly three attempts.

graduation._note: The 200k chase. Graduation progress is the CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH's diamonds against 200,000, confirmed against TikTok Backstage — see the header of lib/graduation.mjs. A creator gets up to three monthly attempts inside their 90 days.
graduation._milestones: Fixed rungs in diamonds still to find: 100k, 50k, 25k, 10k, graduated. Each fires once per creator per month.
graduation._finalPushDays: Inside this many days of month end, a creator still in reach is pinged every morning until they land it or the month runs out.
graduation._finalPushReach: The biggest gap still worth a daily ping in the closing days.
graduation._finalPushStretch: And only when the rate needed is within this multiple of the rate they are actually doing, so the ping is never a lie.

activeness._note: The rank-up incentive's eligibility gate, quoted from the 2026 Fee Policy deck: "Creators who went LIVE for 15 hours on over 7 days that month." Both halves, one calendar month, resets on the 1st.
activeness._days: "over 7 days" means 8 or more; the code adds the one.
activeness._pingWithinDays: Per-creator pings start when the month has this many days left. Earlier than that it is not urgent and the overview covers it.
activeness._minDiamonds: Below this the gate is not what is holding the creator back, and the bonus it protects is worth a few dozen diamonds.
activeness._plausibleHoursPerDay: Used to judge whether the remaining hours can still fit in the remaining days. The network median is 3.2 hours per active day.
activeness._maxPingsPerRun: A channel of a dozen cards gets read. Ninety-six gets scrolled past, and the overview carries everyone either way.

policy._note: The network-level rules from the 2026 Creator Network Policies & Rules deck. See lib/policy.mjs for the definitions and where each number comes from.
policy._cohortMonths: Graduation counts creators who joined in the last N CALENDAR months, not the last 90 days.
policy._graduationFloorRatio: Only creators past this share of the graduation threshold are evaluated at all. The deck: an 80,000 region gives 80,000 x 0.5% = 400. At 200,000 it is 1,000.
policy._tierBands: Diamond tier boundaries from the deck's worked example. The real bands for this region are on LIVE Backstage.
policy._rankUpBaseRatio: Base rank-up bonus: 4% of the creator's monthly Diamonds, 5% with the advanced requirement met.
policy._termination: The inactive-operations rule needs ALL THREE breached: under 60 new creators in 3 months, under 500,000 diamonds in 3 months, and Low tier for 3 consecutive months.

leaderboard._note: Monthly new-creator recruitment board, credited to the creator's Creator Network manager — the export has no separate recruiter column, and the manager is the person who has to make the signing work.
leaderboard._show: Coaches listed. Everyone is counted either way; this is only how many rows the card prints.

growthBoard._note: Coach growth board. Ranked on month-on-month growth pulled toward the network average in proportion to how few creators it rests on, so a big percentage on a small team does not automatically lead.
growthBoard._priorWeight: Creators' worth of network average mixed into every coach's figure. Higher means small teams need to be more extraordinary to top the board.
growthBoard._minComparable: Fewer creators than this in both months and a coach is not ranked at all.
growthBoard._thinBelow: Fewer comparable creators than this and the card marks the row as a small team.

hardestWorker._note: LEAP's Hardest Worker Challenge: the creator-facing board, ranked on LIVE hours streamed this month. Posted daily to the creator server, replacing the day before. On the last day of the month it crowns the winner; on the 1st it starts again from zero.
hardestWorker._show: How many creators the card prints. Everyone who streamed is ranked either way.

creatorWeek._note: Creator of the Week: the creator-facing weekly board. Weeks run Monday to Sunday. It is NOT won by whoever is biggest. Every creator who went LIVE is measured against their OWN recent weeks, pillar by pillar, and ranked on how much they grew; where they came in the network this week counts for a quarter of it, so 'are they growing, and doing well'. Ratios are damped by the network's median baseline, so small numbers cannot fake a tenfold week and a creator starting from zero is finite, not infinite.
creatorWeek._show: How many creators the card prints. Everyone who went LIVE is ranked either way.
creatorWeek._weights: Relative weight of each pillar, set by LEAP: fan club growth counts for most, diamonds and LIVE hours close behind, followers least but never nothing. Each pillar is scored 0 to 1 by position first, so this decides how much that POSITION counts and one enormous week still cannot buy the award.
creatorWeek._growthWeight: How much of the score is growth against the creator's own baseline. This is the thing that stops the same creator winning every week.
creatorWeek._standingWeight: How much of the score is where they came in the network this week. Keeps a creator who tripled from almost nothing from taking it off one who grew strongly on real numbers. Set to 0 to rank on growth alone.
creatorWeek._baselineWeeks: How many of a creator's own previous weeks make up 'their normal'. Three smooths out one freak week without going so far back that a creator who has genuinely levelled up is still measured against who they used to be.
creatorWeek._minStanding: How well a creator has to be doing before their growth counts. 0.75 means the top quarter of the network that week. Expressed as a POSITION, not a number of diamonds, so it scales with the roster and never needs revisiting. Without it a creator 136th of 326 on diamonds came sixth for having grown from almost nothing - a real achievement, and not Creator of the Week. Set to 0 to let anybody win on growth alone.
creatorWeek._minField: The bar only applies once there is a field for it to mean anything. On three creators 'the top quarter' is one creator and the rule picks the winner by itself, so below this many entrants everyone who went LIVE can win.

leaped._note: A creator leaps when their CUMULATIVE totals pass the bar below, at any point in their life with us. It happens once per creator and puts the fee on that month's payroll. Recorded permanently the first time it is seen, so a re-run or a config change can never move anybody's pay.
leaped._monthOverride: Months whose leap bonus is taken from the Recruitment 26/27 sheet instead of computed. This system started watching on 31 August and a leap is a LIFETIME 5 hours and 5,000 diamonds, so for any month before it had a full history it cannot tell who crossed the bar THAT month from who had crossed it long ago. LEAP worked September out by hand and the sheet's own figures are the answer: per coach, in pounds, summing to the 400 in its September column. From October on there is enough history to compute it, so no month should need an entry here again.
leaped._closeWithin: Creators this near the diamond half of the bar are named on the overview, so a coach can push them over it.
leaped._maxCardsPerRun: Up to this many leaps get their own card; more than that in one run are digested into one.
leaped._excluded: Partner agencies are not LEAP payroll, so monitoring.ignoreGroups applies here too.

rankUp._note: The rank-up task. A creator's tier is set by LAST month's diamonds and cannot move; ranking out of it this month pays the coach 1% of the creator's whole month. See lib/tiers.mjs for how the table and the rule were verified against the WAGES CALCUATOR tab.
rankUp._advanced: Base or Advanced bonus ratio. Advanced, verified against Backstage's own per-creator rank-up page on 30 September 2026: coregaming2811 458,691 diamonds showed $344.01, sur3shot 314,254 showed $235.69, samboogames 214,578 showed $160.93, .yas_xoxoo 172,494 showed $129.37 - every one of them diamonds x $0.01 x 0.075 to the cent, and none of them x 0.065. This sets what TIKTOK pays LEAP; the coach's own share is a flat 1% of diamond dollars and does not move with it.
rankUp._coachSharePerDiamondUsd: What the coach gets on a creator who ranks up: $0.01 a diamond at a 1% share. Same number as revenue.rankUpPerDiamondUsd, kept here so the chase figures and the pay block cannot drift apart.
rankUp._stretch: A near-miss counts as in reach only if the daily rate needed is within this multiple of the creator's own rate so far. Two means we will ask somebody to double, not to triple.
rankUp._tiers: Tier thresholds and the rank-up ratio, from TikTok's own table. Tier 10 pays nothing, so there is nothing above it to chase. The maintenance ratios are NOT here: Backstage shows a second column for them and we have never been given it, so tier maintenance is reported and deliberately valued at zero.

revenue._note: Rough monthly earnings at the bottom of each team summary, using the component names from the Recruitment 26/27 sheet. Payments land on the 15th of the following month, so this is the month being built.
revenue._baseWage: The sheet calls this EXTRA REVENUE. There is no default: a coach who is not listed below is not on a fixed amount, and inventing one for them is worse than showing nothing.
revenue._baseWageByCoach: Read off the Recruitment 26/27 sheet's forward column (September onward). Most are on 150; Sureshot 350, Colesy 250, CamB 100.
revenue._hideEarningsFor: Coaches who see their team's card without a wage on it. For somebody doing the work before the arrangement is settled - a trial, a hand-over - where an estimated wage would create an expectation nobody promised. Their figures are still computed, so the directors' numbers and the network totals stay whole; only the display is withheld. Remove the address to turn it back on.
revenue._rankUpPerDiamondUsd: Rank ups, which Recruitment 26/27 calls ALPHA GROUP TASK BONUS. The WAGES CALCUATOR tab's COACH column: diamonds x $0.01 a diamond x a 1% share. Recomputing all 174 creator rows across February to July reproduces both that column and its POUND column with zero mismatches. WHO it is paid on lives in the rankUp block below, not here.
revenue._managerPerDiamondUsd: The manager diamond share: the recruiter commission formula, 0.00005 USD a diamond, applied across the coach's whole roster. At roughly $1 to GBP 0.75 that is the 0.0000375 a diamond quoted in GBP. UNVERIFIED, unlike rank ups - the population is an open question and needs a July creator export to settle. See the header of lib/revenue.mjs.
revenue._usdToGbp: The finance sheet's own FX cell, read off the WAGES CALCUATOR tab. Its per-row POUND column reproduces exactly at this rate; the frozen monthly totals in Recruitment 26/27 were each struck at the FX of their own day, so they drift from it by up to 2 percent.
revenue._incremental: The manager diamond share, which Recruitment 26/27 calls MANAGER DIAMOND %. Solved from LEAP's own sheet and exact to the penny for all ten coaches in September: roster diamonds x $0.01 x TikTok's incremental rate x the coach's unlock x FX. TikTok's rate moves with network volume - 8% in September on 29.0m diamonds, about 4% in August on 25.3m - and LEAP's instruction is that the BOARDS always quote 5%, never the live rate, so a coach's card never promises a number a quiet month cannot pay.

incremental._boardRate: What the cards quote. Held at 5% on purpose: under-promise, and a high month is a surprise rather than a card that lied.
incremental._actualRate: What TikTok actually paid for the month, for reconciling against the finance sheet. Only read by the CLI, never by a card.
incremental._goalBonus: Added once for hitting the group's diamond goal and once for hitting the recruiter goal, so 10/15/20.
incremental._actualRateProof: September's 8% is not an estimate: StaySocial's Backstage contribution of $124.99 less $18.79 of activeness leaves $106.20, and 132,754 diamonds x $0.01 x 8% is $106.20 exactly.

revenue._activeness: TikTok's THIRD incentive, beside rank-up and incremental, and the one this system missed until October. diamonds x $0.01 x a ratio set by the creator's ACTIVENESS LEVEL for the month. Verified to the cent against Backstage's own per-creator page for StaySocial in September: 7 of 7 rows.
revenue._activenessLevels: The level comes from valid go LIVE days AND LIVE duration for the month, pro-rated for a part-month and with static LIVE excluded (2026 Positive Incentives deck). It is NOT in the creator export, so it is carried here per month from Backstage. Levels 2, 3 and 4 are observed. Levels 1 and 5 are NOT confirmed and are marked as such: no LEAP creator has been seen on either.
revenue._goals: Backstage's monthly goals, per coach, read off the Group goals page on the 1st. diamonds is the whole group's target; recruits is the recruiter target. Each one hit adds goalBonus to that coach's unlock. A coach with no entry sits on the base 10% and their card shows no goal line, which is the honest default: it reads as 'no target set', not as two goals missed.

cases._interactive: true when coaches can click buttons (bot mode). false changes escalation to a data signal and closes stale cases, since nothing else would.

monitoring._ignoreGroups: Teams nobody is coaching. Their data still accrues, but no case is opened and nothing is posted. Matching ignores case and spacing.
monitoring._goneAfterMissedSnapshots: How many exports in a row a creator can be missing before the system treats them as gone. LEAP's rule is that absence from the Creator data export IS departure, so this is 1. TikTok lists a leaver in its quit section only sometimes; the rest vanish with no row at all, and until this existed nothing noticed - quitOn stayed null, every filter still counted them, and the rolling 28-day windows kept them on their team's summary for weeks. Reappearing clears it.
monitoring._goneMaxShareOfRoster: The safety valve on acting that fast. Setting quitOn also closes a creator's open cases as lost, and a truncated or half-written export would do that to the whole network at once - which no reappearance undoes. A snapshot missing more than this share of the live roster is treated as a bad file: nobody is marked and nothing is counted against anybody. Real daily churn is 0 to 2 creators (0.2%); the month-end clear-out that prompted this was 2.6%.
monitoring._goneShareMinRoster: The valve above only applies once the roster is this big. A share means nothing on a tiny network: with three creators, one leaving is 33% and is plainly not a half-written file.

posts._note: Recurring posts that keep only their current version: each day's card removes the one before it, so a channel holds what is true now rather than a month of stale copies. Per-creator cards are work items and are never replaced. Set any of these false to keep every post.
posts._boards: The two monthly boards replace within a month only — the closing board of each month is the result and survives into the next.
posts._hardestWorker: The creator-facing board is the one that does NOT keep a closing edition: it is asked to clear on the 1st, so each new month's board removes the last one outright.
posts._creatorWeek: Creator of the Week clears the same way the Hardest Worker board does, on Monday rather than the 1st: Sunday's winner is removed by the new week's first board.
posts._partners: The partner revenue card replaces within a month only, like the other monthly boards: the closing card of each month is a settlement record a partner will look back at.

activation._note: Creators who never started. Excluded from decline rules by design, which otherwise leaves a third of the network invisible.

programmes._note: Network-level findings posted weekly to the management channel. A programme decision, not 400 conversations.

avatars._note: Off by default. A resolver that cannot find the handle renders as a broken-image icon in Discord, which looks worse than no picture at all. Set enabled true to try urlTemplate, or fill manual with {"username": "https://..."} for the creators you care about.

growth._note: The daily per-team summary. Thresholds are measured from LEAP's own data, not chosen — see the header of lib/teamsummary.mjs for the table they came from.
growth._liveDaysTarget: LIVE days in 28 where the network turns from shrinking to growing. Above it 59% of creators grew last month; below it 31%.
growth._fanClubUp: Active fan club growth over 14 days that precedes diamond growth. Creators above it grew 66% of the time.
growth._chaseFloor: A creator projected below this share of 200k is not chasing it, and listing them buries the ones who are.

starlight._comment: TikTok's Star Light Agency Tournament, 1-31 Oct 2026. Outside from..to there is nothing to chase, so the card stops posting rather than going stale.
starlight._daily: The short list the card leads with. messagesPerDay is how many names a coach gets; cooldownDays is how long before somebody can reappear, which is what makes it a rotation; minWorth is the floor below which a message is not worth sending.
starlight._onCourseOdds: At or above this measured chance of reaching 10 days on their own, a creator is listed as on course and kept off the chase list. Messaging them is the comfortable call and buys nothing.
starlight._interaction: TikTok scores active interaction and the export has no column for it. Measured against Backstage's own score on 34 LIVE creators, gifts per LIVE hour separates it at 0.84 AUC where LIVE hours and days do not separate at all (0.51, 0.53). The cut at 20 calls 82% of them right. See the header of lib/starlight.mjs.

partners._note: Partner agencies under the Agency Partner Programme Agreement. They recruit and manage their own creators, who stay contractually under LEAP's TikTok registration, and LEAP settles a share of the agency revenue those creators generate (clauses 2 and 5). Separate from monitoring.ignoreGroups, which keeps their creators off LEAP's coaching boards — that is right, because nobody at LEAP coaches them, and it must not keep them off the revenue card, because the money is real.
partners._tiers: Clause 5's revenue-share ladder. The tier is a monthly judgement LEAP makes on growth, compliance, retention and contribution, so it is set here rather than computed.
partners._agencies: group is the Group value as it appears in the creator export. tier must match a name in the ladder above.

agencies.name: Stay Social
agencies._levels: Activeness levels from Backstage, per month, per creator. Refresh monthly from Revenue > Incentives > Contributions > By creator. Where the current month has no entry, the most recent month is carried forward and the card says it is doing so.

partners._useActualRate: A partner is settled on the agency revenue their creators actually generated, so their card uses TikTok's real monthly incremental rate where we know it rather than the 5% the coach boards quote. Quoting 5% to a partner settled at 8% understates them by over a third. Falls back to the board rate, and the card always names the rate it used.
